shots.name: 1 · Extreme wide set
shots.purpose: establishing: the horses waiting in open country, the riders running in from the edge of frame
shots.why: The establishing frame answers 'where are we' so every later close-up can be placed in space. The 28mm wide lens exaggerates depth, so the space around the subject becomes part of the drama. The opening wide gives the destination and direction, the tracking sprint sells urgency, and the insert-to-vault cut on action makes the mount feel faster than it is. The side track at gallop keeps screen direction constant, and the long-lens wide lets them go, which is the release the sequence has been building toward. Rule: establish the start point and the destination direction in one wide before going close, because speed only reads against a known space; inserts without geography are just noise.
alternatives: Avoid cutting between shots where the runners travel opposite screen directions: it reads as a reversal or a second chase.
Hold it longer than feels comfortable if the scene needs more weight; wides earn their duration.
